label: Philip Schneider
narrative: Philip Schneider supplied every specific number in the modern Dulce claim and none of them can be traced past him. In a lecture at Post Falls, Idaho on 8 May 1995 he said he had been 'involved in building an addition to the deep underground military base at Dulce', that his job was 'to go down the holes and check the rock samples, and recommend the explosive[s]', that the base 'goes down seven levels and over 2.5 miles deep', and that in a cavern there he shot two aliens, after which the thirty people already underground and about forty more who came down were killed. He arrived late: Norio Hayakawa's chronology places him outside the initial rumours entirely and dates his emergence to 1995, when the Dulce story was already about fifteen years old. WHAT COULD NOT BE ESTABLISHED IS RECORDED HERE AND NOT ONLY IN THE GAPS. No employment of Philip Schneider by anybody, ever, was documented by this board: no employer record, no contract, no clearance record, no payroll. The attribution to Morrison Knudsen, the Corps of Engineers and the Navy rests on a contributor-written biography attached to his Find a Grave memorial and on his own lectures, and a contributor-written memorial biography is not a record of employment. His death is likewise unresolved: the memorial record gives 11 January 1996 in Clackamas County, Oregon, while the date in circulation, tied to the discovery of the body, is 17 January 1996, and NO DEATH CERTIFICATE, MEDICAL EXAMINER'S REPORT OR POLICE REPORT WAS OPENED. The suicide ruling, the ligature and his former wife's letter contesting the finding are all in circulation and none of it is carried as a claim here. The one genuinely documented element of the Schneider story is his father: Captain Otto Oscar Schneider, US Navy, 22 January 1906 to 13 May 1993, on a Find a Grave memorial originally created by the US Veterans Affairs Office. The rank and the dates are real; the narrative attached to the same page, a captured U-boat commander repatriated into US Naval Intelligence, Operation Crossroads and the Philadelphia Experiment, is contributor prose and none of it is asserted. It matters only because Philip Schneider's own claim leaned on his father's standing, and the standing is real while the stories about it are not documented by anything opened here.
